newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end higher on stronger CBOT.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end higher on stronger CBOT.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures ended higher on Monday, reflecting the Chicago market's price rallies on Friday, traders said.
Prices were up 10 to 200 yen, with the benchmark January 1998 contract up 90 yen at 15,190 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 49,700 lots, and open interest as of January 24 totalled 591,519 lots.

All months gained from the opening, as individual investors started buying actively, traders said. "The soybean market's recent price rallies also encouraged investors to buy corn," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot March corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was traded at $2.72 per bushel at 0755 GMT, against $2.72-3/4 at Friday's close.
The spot March soybean contract on the overnight trading system was at $7.50 a bushel, up from $7.47-1/2 at Friday's close.
